jobs.title: Director, IT & Data Business Partner
jobs.description:
About The Job

The Director, IT & Data Business Partner (BP) serves as the strategic liaison between Danone Canada’s enterprise functions and the IT & Data organization. This role partners closely with stakeholders across Commercial, Sales, Marketing, eCommerce, Insights, Strategy & Transformation, Operations, Supply Chain, Research & Innovation (R&I), Quality, Food Safety & Compliance (QFS), Cycles & Procurement (C&P), Finance, HR, Legal, Customer Care, and supporting functions to understand business priorities, translate needs into technology and data solutions, and drive value realization through product adoption and delivery.

The Director BP is responsible for aligning Canada business objectives with IT & Data product roadmaps, ensuring that strategic initiatives are prioritized, funded, governed, and successfully executed. Acting as a trusted advisor, this role connects Canadian business leaders with Product Groups, Product Owners, chapters, regional teams, and global technology partners to accelerate innovation, improve enterprise performance, and support business transformation.

This position plays a critical role in driving business engagement, ensuring service continuity, strengthening cyber and data governance, and maximizing the value delivered through technology, data, analytics, automation, AI, digital products, and enterprise platforms across Danone Canada.

Key Responsibilities

Business Partnership & Strategic Alignment

Serve as the primary IT & Data partner for Danone Canada leaders across enterprise functions, including Commercial, Sales, Marketing, eCommerce, Insights, Strategy & Transformation, Operations, Supply Chain, R&I, QFS, C&P, Finance, HR, Legal, Customer Care, and supporting functions.
Develop a deep understanding of Canada business priorities, challenges, market dynamics, and strategic objectives.
Translate business needs into technology, data, analytics, automation, AI, and enterprise platform opportunities and connect stakeholders with the appropriate Product Groups and subject matter experts.
Facilitate prioritization of Canadian business initiatives and ensure alignment with global, regional, and local IT & Data strategies.
Build and maintain strong relationships with business stakeholders to foster trust, collaboration, accountable ownership, and value creation.

Portfolio & Roadmap Management

Manage the Canada IT & Data product and project portfolio in partnership with Product Groups, chapters, regional IT & Data teams, and global technology partners.
Develop and maintain an enterprise Canada roadmap that aligns technology capabilities with business priorities across the full value chain.
Support business case development, CAPEX/OPEX planning, demand intake, and investment prioritization for strategic initiatives.
Ensure visibility, alignment, and communication of priorities across Canada business leadership, regional IT & Data, Product Groups, and delivery teams.

Value Creation & Business Outcomes

Identify opportunities to leverage technology, digital capabilities, enterprise platforms, data, analytics, automation, and AI to improve business performance and enterprise outcomes across Danone Canada.
Drive adoption of products and solutions to maximize business value realization, including self-service analytics, data products, Copilot and AI capabilities, workflow automation, and fit-for-purpose tools.
Monitor business satisfaction and continuously identify opportunities to improve service delivery, user experience, process efficiency, and decision-making.
Support business continuity by partnering with Product Groups, IT4U, cybersecurity, infrastructure, data, and application teams to address risks, escalations, critical issues, and local market needs.

Product Delivery & Transformation

Collaborate with Product Owners and Product Group Leaders throughout the product lifecycle, from ideation through feasibility, funding, delivery, deployment, adoption, and continuous improvement.
Ensure business requirements, success metrics, value assumptions, governance needs, data ownership, and expected outcomes are clearly defined.
Promote agile ways of working and support effective product ownership, demand governance, business case discipline, and adoption practices.
Lead cross-functional alignment across Canada, regional, and global teams to support successful delivery of strategic initiatives across commercial, operations, supply chain, finance, HR, digital, data, and supporting functions.

Stakeholder Management & Communication

Act as a trusted advisor and advocate for Danone Canada within the IT & Data organization.
Provide regular updates on roadmap progress, business priorities, key initiatives, risks, funding needs, service topics, and opportunities.
Facilitate discussions and decision-making across multiple stakeholders and functions, including Canadian leadership forums, Product Groups, project steercos, and business-led governance forums.
Promote continuous improvement and strengthen collaboration between Canada business teams and IT & Data teams, positioning IT & Data as a strategic partner and co-owner of business outcomes.

Compensation, Benefits & Hiring Transparency

The annual base salary range for this position is $140,000 to $190,000 CAD. The final salary offered will be determined by factors such as relevant experience and qualifications, internal equity and external market conditions.

Danone Canada also offers a competitive short-term incentive bonus and a comprehensive benefits package, including group insurance, group retirement plans, wellbeing account, flexible time off, true hybrid work environment, paid parental leave, and other attractive options.

As part of our commitment to transparency in our hiring practices, we may use AI-enabled tools at certain stages of the recruitment process. However, all final hiring decisions are made by people.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

About You

Education & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Data & Analytics, Engineering, Business Systems, Business Administration, or a related field.
7+ years of experience in technology, digital, data, business partnering, product management, enterprise applications, or related business transformation roles.
Experience working across commercial, sales, marketing, eCommerce, strategy, operations, supply chain, procurement, quality, R&I, finance, HR, or related enterprise functions preferred.
Proven experience managing stakeholders and influencing decisions across multiple organizational levels, including senior business leaders.
Experience participating in product-centric, agile, digital transformation, data governance, AI, automation, or enterprise technology environments.

Skills & Competencies

Strong business partnering and stakeholder management capabilities across enterprise functions.
Ability to translate business challenges into technology, data, analytics, automation, AI, and enterprise platform solutions.
Excellent communication, facilitation, change management, and influencing skills.
Strong project, portfolio, roadmap, demand, funding, and prioritization management capabilities.
Solid understanding of product management, agile delivery methodologies, data governance, cybersecurity, enterprise applications, and service management.
Ability to manage complex situations and navigate ambiguity in a fast-paced, matrixed environment.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a focus on delivering measurable business outcomes.
Demonstrated ability to work effectively across local, regional, and global teams.

Assets

Experience within CPG, FMCG, manufacturing, retail, commercial, supply chain, or enterprise business environments.
Understanding of enterprise data and analytics, retailer data, commercial platforms, digital marketing and eCommerce tools, finance and supporting function processes, supply chain systems, quality systems, operational analytics, procurement platforms, automation, AI, and enterprise business processes.
Experience working in a global matrix organization and partnering with local market leadership, regional IT & Data teams, Product Groups, and global technology teams.

About us

Danone Canada is part of Danone, the largest certified B Corp™ in the world, proudly using our business as a force for good – creating value for people, communities, and the planet. Guided by our long-standing mission to bring health through food to as many people as possible
, we embed this purpose into every aspect of our operations.

Our workforce spans the country, with two headquarters (Boucherville, QC, and Toronto, ON), a production facility in Boucherville, and various remote work sites across the provinces.

When you join us, you’ll work with some of the best-known food and beverage brands in the world, including Oikos, Activia, Two Good, evian, Silk, International Delight, So Delicious Dairy Free and STōK Cold Brew Coffee.

We offer a competitive and comprehensive total rewards package, including group insurance plans, retirement programs, well-being resources, parental leave, and development opportunities. Plus, a true hybrid work environment and flexible time off, empowering you to balance your personal and professional life.

At Danone, inclusion and diversity are at the heart of who we are. We celebrate unique perspectives and are committed to building a workplace where everyone feels valued, respected, and empowered to thrive. We encourage applications from everyone and offer accommodations upon request to ensure equitable access for all candidates.

Join us and help shape a healthier, more sustainable world. One Planet. One Health. BY YOU.

jobs.description:
You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients - who are at the heart of everything we do.

At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

Job Description:

The Director, IT Application Audit
is responsible for the oversight and delivery of risk-based internal audits across the Business Group Chief Information Officer (CIO) application portfolio and technology in Canada and the United States, and when needed in Asia. The role provides independent assurance and advisory support over business applications, data, digital delivery, enabling platforms and associated technology and cyber risk management practices. The scope includes First and Second Line activities and support for integrated business audits with significant technology components.

Reporting to the Assistant Vice President, IT Audit, the Director leads assigned members of a geographically dispersed audit team and is accountable for high-quality audit delivery, stakeholder relationships, people development and continuous improvement of audit practices.

What You Will Be Doing

The scope of responsibilities includes for assigned areas the operational delivery of all IT audit work, audit plan development and coverage, IT audit universe risk assessments to ensure the adequacy of audit coverage of key risks, as well as relationship management with clients and management of the audit team.
Identify emerging and heightened risk related to technology and cyber security in applications and technology processes, digital transformation and modernization, AI and data.
Contribute to the development of Audit strategy and direction, and talent initiatives.
Continuously improve audit delivery and quality through increased use of AI, data analytics and innovation.
Plan and direct audits and special engagements following Sun Life’s Audit methodology; deliver audit reports and findings that clearly articulate the position of risks and issues.
Provide subject matter expertise as it relates to technology, cyber and information risk management processes to other audit teams.
Provide leadership in discussions of risk assessment, internal control and audit findings with clients.
Actively stay engaged in the latest technologies, regulations and cyber trends.
Manage multiple engagements and priorities concurrently, including scope, resourcing, milestones, quality review, stakeholder communication and issue escalation.
Influence management to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of operations, risk management practices and the control environment with respect to technology, cyber and information risk management.
Lead an audit team with a focus on building and maintaining a high-performing team of auditors, including the recruitment, administration, development and retention of staff through strong leadership and coaching.

What You Need to Succeed

6-8+ years of leadership experience in IT, IT Audit, or related risk management or governance/control functions.
University degree or equivalent experience, plus recognized auditing (e.g., CISA, CPA, CIA), or security (e.g., CISSP) designations/certifications.
Previous people management experience, with demonstrated employee engagement results.
This role is based in Toronto and the individual is expected to work in a hybrid environment (virtual and in the office). Occasional travel to the US and rarely to Asia may be required.
In-depth knowledge of audit methodologies, system development methodologies, control frameworks, risk practices and regulatory requirements.
Exceptional understanding of application development & maintenance, technology and cyber processes, risks and controls.
In-depth knowledge of the latest application technology and security trends, best practices and industry standards.
Proficiency in cyber security risk and control frameworks and information risk management frameworks.
Strong working knowledge of risks affecting the insurance industry and financial institutions.
Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and succinctly and effectively deliver key messages verbally and in writing.
Effective listener who remains open and receptive to various viewpoints.
Confident presenter and facilitator with strong interpersonal and leadership skills to work with senior management at all levels.
Effective influencer and negotiator with the ability to effectively manage and resolve conflicts across all levels of management.
Professional presence and the ability to navigate through a matrix organization.
Critical thinker who can assess risk and controls and identify issues.
Flexible, organized and able to effectively manage multiple engagements and priorities concurrently.
Strategic thinker who can see and share the big picture while retaining attention to detail.
Demonstrated ability to identify opportunities to use AI and data analytics to enhance the depth and breadth of audit coverage.
Demonstrated ability to work and lead effectively in diverse environments and cultures across multiple office locations.

The Base Pay range is for the primary location for which the job is posted. It may vary depending on the work location of the successful candidate or other factors. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Sun Life employees participate in various incentive plans, payment under which is discretionary and subject to individual and company performance. Certain sales focused roles have sales incentive plans based on individual or group sales results.

Diversity and inclusion have always been at the core of our values at Sun Life. A diverse workforce with wide perspectives and creative ideas benefits our Clients, the communities where we operate and all of us as colleagues. We welcome applications from qualified individuals from all backgrounds.

Persons with disabilities who need accommodation in the application process, or those needing job postings in an alternative format, may e-mail a request to thebrightside@sunlife.com.

We are proud to be a hybrid organization that offers our employees the choice and flexibility to work from both the office and virtually based on the needs of the business, our Clients and you.

We may use artificial intelligence to support candidate sourcing, screening, interview scheduling.

We thank all applicants for showing an interest in this position. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: VP, Sales - Canada
jobs.description:
Job Description

About us

With over 200 brands sold in nearly 180 countries, Diageo is home to some of the world’s most iconic drinks. From Crown Royal and Guinness to Tanqueray, Smirnoff and Don Julio, we craft brands chosen for life’s moments — from everyday connections to landmark celebrations.

Bring your talent, curiosity and ambition, and strive for your personal best alongside people who challenge, support and learn from each other. Together, as one outstanding team, we keep learning, improving and raising the bar for our brands, our business and each other.

Join us and play your part in making life’s moments mean a little more.

About The Function

Sales is where our brands meet the real world.

This team builds the relationships that bring our products to life, partnering closely with customers across markets, channels and occasions to make sure our brands are part of moments that matter.

It’s a dynamic, people-focused environment where curiosity, commercial thinking and strong relationships make the difference. You’ll have the opportunity to grow your network, develop your skills and see the direct impact of your work every day.

About This Role

VP, Channel & Customer, Canada

Location: Toronto

Function: Commercial – Channel, Customer & Sales

Manager: President, Canada

________________________

Lead the Canada commercial agenda by bringing Commercial Strategy & Planning and the Liquor Control Board, Private/Chain Retail, and On-Premise channel teams under one accountable leader. The role owns the customer-back strategy, channel choices, revenue growth plan, route-to-market model, and execution standards required to deliver profitable growth. As a member of the Canada Leadership Team, the VP converts portfolio and category ambition into customer plans and disciplined execution across Canada’s complex provincial and regulatory environment.

Key Responsibilities

Set the integrated Canada channel and customer strategy, defining where and how the business will win across Liquor Control Boards, Private/Chain Retail, On-Premise, and emerging routes to market.
Lead the Commercial Strategy & Planning Director and the Sales Directors for Liquor Control Boards, Private/Chain Retail, and On-Premise, creating one commercial agenda, clear accountabilities, and consistent performance routines.
Own commercial performance across net sales, depletions, market share, distribution, assortment, execution, trade investment, gross margin, and customer service; connect customer plans and commercial assumptions into AOP, IBP, forecasting, and risk/opportunity management.
Build senior relationships with priority customers and commercial partners; strengthen joint business planning, executive engagement, negotiation quality, and customer satisfaction.
Partner with the VP Marketing and Category & Brand teams to translate portfolio, category, innovation, and brand priorities into customer-back strategies, channel selling stories, Pictures of Success, and field-ready activation plans.
Lead the Revenue Growth Management agenda across pricing, Price Pack Architecture, promotion, mix, assortment, trade terms, and investment effectiveness, supported by strong commercial analytics and governance.
Manage the route-to-market, broker, and coverage model – focusing on improving outlet reach, service, productivity, and execution across direct and indirect sales resources.
Partner with Finance, Supply, Customer Service, Legal, Corporate Relations, and HR to commercialize innovation, resolve customer and service issues, manage regulatory complexity, and ensure strong governance and responsible selling.
Build a high-performing, inclusive commercial organization through talent selection, coaching, succession planning, capability development, and a one-team culture focused on customers and results.

Key Outputs

Canada channel and customer strategy, annual commercial plan, and multi-year growth roadmap.
Channel strategies and execution plans for Liquor Control Boards, Private/Chain Retail, and On-Premise.
Priority customer joint business plans, executive relationship plans, and customer performance scorecards.
Revenue Growth Management, pricing, Price Pack Architecture, promotion, mix, and trade-investment recommendations.
Channel/category selling stories, Pictures of Success, and activation standards developed with Marketing and Commercial Strategy & Planning.
Route-to-market, broker, coverage, and service plans with clear productivity and execution measures.

Beacon is building the essential technology infrastructure for the everyday economy: the businesses, organizations, and services that make real life work, and that mainstream tech has largely left behind. We acquire, operate, and grow vertical market software companies. They are niche, founder-built businesses serving industries that are often overlooked and too profitable to ignore.

We buy great businesses, invest in their continued growth, and hold them permanently, accelerating that growth with an AI-native platform built specifically for vertical market software. No mandate to cut, flip, or roll up into something unrecognizable.

We are not a financial firm. We are technology entrepreneurs and operators who believe the most important businesses in the world are already running quietly in industries most people never think about. Our job is to find them, support the people who built them, and make them better.

Beacon is backed by a diverse base of investors, with $550M+ raised to date, including General Catalyst, Lightspeed, D1 Capital, CPMG, the family offices of the founders of Stripe, DoorDash, and Ramp, and evergreen funds built for the long game.

The Role:

VieFund is a Beacon company with remote teams in Toronto, Ottawa and Vietnam. Its software is the system of record for mutual fund, segregated fund and GIC dealers in Canada: advisor tools, trades, settlements, account bookkeeping, and reporting, connected to the industry through FundServ, CANNEX and exempt-market dealer networks.

We are looking for the next technical leader of VieFund. You will own the platform end to end and work closely with the current technical team in Ottawa and Vietnam to build deep knowledge of the product, the dealers, and the operating rhythm. In the first year, you keep every dealer running through tax season, the FundServ standard change, and year-end, and you draw up the plan to move the platform off its on-prem footing, modernize it and add more value to customers with AI. You are the person who understands what is going on quickly and decides what to do about it.

You will be the technical owner of a profitable, long-held product with real customers and real seasonal deadlines, with Beacon's engineering leadership behind you and the mandate to make it better.

What You'll Do:

Own the VieFund platform end to end: architecture, codebase, database, releases, and production operations.
Build and maintain complete documentation of system behaviour, dealer configurations, and operational runbooks.
Maintain and evolve VieFund's FundServ integration, including annual standard upgrades, certification, and resolution of transaction and reconciliation issues with counterparties.
Design, build, and maintain the transaction processing, account bookkeeping, and reporting logic at the core of the product, ensuring accuracy and auditability.
Act as the final escalation point for client-facing technical issues; diagnose root causes and implement durable fixes.
Plan and deliver around the industry calendar, including tax season, RRSP and RRIF deadlines, and regulatory and standards changes.
Define and execute the technical roadmap, including the migration from on-prem infrastructure to the cloud and the adoption of modern engineering and AI-assisted development practices.
Manage production environments across hosted and client-managed Windows Server deployments, including backups, patching, security, and uptime.
Partner with hosting providers, dealers, and internal stakeholders to deliver reliable service and clear communication.
Hire, mentor, and lead engineers and contractors as the team grows.

What We Are Looking For:

Must have:

Deep, hands-on FundServ experience. Not just sending and receiving files: you have lived through the yearly standard change, you have debugged failures that originated at other vendors or at the fund, and you know how to work the problem when the documentation does not help.
Mutual fund transaction accounting and reporting. You understand the bookkeeping behind trades, settlements, distributions, and corrections, and you have fixed it when it was wrong.
Expert in .NET, MSSQL, and T-SQL. Much of the dealer-specific logic lives in stored procedures and scripts. You are at home there.
Windows Server management. You can stand up, patch, back up, and troubleshoot production servers, including ones you do not control.
Able to be in Ottawa at least bi-weekly for the first six months as part of onboarding. Knowledge transfer happens in person.
Judgment that does not need a committee. You will often be the only engineer in the room.
Easy to work with. Dealers call when something is wrong. The team has to trust you with the product.
Daily use of AI coding tools, and the drive to bring them into a codebase that has none.

Nice to have:

Experience migrating an on-prem system to the cloud, and the judgement to sequence it without breaking customers.
FIX protocol, for the ETF side of the business. Small part of the work, easy to pick up, but a head start helps.
Experience at a Canadian wealth or dealer platform (back office, transfer agency, or dealer software).
Experience replacing a long-tenured sole owner of a system.

Location and Working Arrangement:

Remote with ability to meet with with the teams in Ottawa and/or Toronto, Ontario. During onboarding must be able to be in Ottawa bi-weekly for the first 6 months.
Some work happens outside dealer business hours so it does not disrupt their day. Expect occasional evenings and weekends, heaviest around the seasonal peaks. Reducing this is part of the modernization mandate, but it is the reality today.

Our Values at Beacon Software

Humility: We acknowledge that the path to getting to the right answer involves being wrong along the way. We have strong beliefs which are weakly held. We actively seek new ideas and believe we can learn from anyone at any time.
Honesty: We are truth seeking in our approach to business problems. Business is a repeat game and we believe that human relationships generate alpha. We understand that trust is earned over a lifetime and can be lost in an instant.
Hunger: We play to win. We hold ourselves to high standards and will not be outworked. We take pride in having a deep sense of responsibility to ourselves, each other, our partners, and our customers. We believe to whom much is given much is expected.
Horizon: We seek to build a generational software company. This will take decades. We manage our expectations and those of our partners to take advantage of the 8th wonder of the world - compounding growth.

How We Use AI in Our Hiring Process:
To ensure transparency, we want candidates to know that Beacon Software uses Artificial Intelligence and AI-enabled tools to assist with screening, reviewing, organizing and highlighting profiles and applications that match the key requirements for each role.

AI does not make hiring decisions:
Every application is reviewed by a member of our team, and all decisions throughout the process are made by humans. We use AI to support efficiency and consistency, not to replace human judgment. We are committed to a fair, thoughtful, and equitable experience for every candidate.

OpenText is a global leader in information management, where innovation, creativity, and collaboration are the key components of our corporate culture. As Director of Product Management for Security Operations and Digital Forensics, you will own the vision, strategy, execution, and business outcomes for both Lines of Business within the OpenText Portfolio Business Unit. You will shape investment priorities across on-premises, private and sovereign cloud, and OpenText-hosted private-cloud SaaS offerings. By connecting customer needs and market opportunities in SOC modernization, threat detection and response, cyber resilience, digital investigations, compliance, and examiner productivity, you will strengthen OpenText's position as a trusted provider of Security Operations and Digital Forensics solutions.

Ownership of the vision, strategy, investment priorities, and business performance for the Security Operations and Digital Forensics Lines of Business.

Decision authority for product lifecycle governance, roadmap prioritization, feature investments, pricing, packaging, partner decisions, release readiness, compliance, security, certifications, localization, and communications.

Leadership and development of a high-performing team of Product Managers and senior product professionals, with accountability for hiring, coaching, performance management, succession planning, and leadership development.
A highly visible role requiring strategic agility, critical analysis, innovation, resilience, and the ability to influence senior leaders, customers, analysts, and partners in a complex global environment.

What You Need to Succeed

10+ years of progressive Product Management experience in enterprise software, cybersecurity, digital investigations, or related markets, including significant leadership of Product Managers and complex portfolios.
Minimum 5 years of managerial leadership experience with demonstrated success developing high-performing teams and future product leaders.
Deep expertise in Security Operations, SIEM, Security Analytics, Threat Detection and Response, SOC workflows, SOAR, log analytics, and threat intelligence.
Strong understanding of Digital Forensics, DFIR, investigative workflows, forensic acquisition and analysis, evidence management, and chain of custody.
Proven track record owning portfolio vision and strategy while delivering measurable outcomes in revenue growth, retention, cloud adoption, and profitability.
Experience leading SaaS transformation, cloud modernization, containerized platforms, and enterprise-scale portfolios.
Demonstrated success influencing executive stakeholders and driving alignment across global cross-functional organizations.
Strong business acumen, with the ability to balance strategic investments, customer commitments, engineering priorities, and commercial objectives, and translate technical concepts into compelling business strategies.
Bachelor's degree in a technical discipline or equivalent experience. An advanced degree and relevant certifications such as CISSP, GCFE, GCFA, EnCE, GREM, or equivalent are desirable.

OpenText is more than a corporation—it’s a global community built on trust, character, and purpose. Here, we act ethically, care deeply about people, and always put our clients first. We help teams succeed through collaboration, tackle challenges with resilience, and innovate with intention.

Join us on our mission to drive positive change through privacy, technology, and teamwork. At OpenText, we don’t just have a culture—we live our values. Choose us because you want to be part of a company that empowers you to make a meaningful impact.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
A Little Bit About Us

Founded in Vancouver in 2016, FORM is the sports technology company behind the award-winning FORM Smart Swim Goggles. Since launching in 2019, our goggles have earned global recognition, including Red Dot, iF Design, and Global Triathlon awards, and are trusted by professional athletes, age-group triathletes, and swimmers looking to get better.
We're a talented, tight-knit team that's fun to work with and serious about building great products. Together, we bring decades of consumer product experience spanning sports eyewear, interface design, and activity-tracking algorithms.
To learn more, visit formswim.com

The Opportunity

Reporting to the CEO, you'll own FORM's finance function end to end. You'll start by learning how our accounting function runs today, then partner with the team to strengthen controls and streamline processes as we grow. From there, you'll lean into financial modelling and become a strategic partner to the executive team.
You'll work directly alongside the CEO, with access to our fractional CFO for mentorship. You'll have real ownership over how FORM plans, reports, and grows, and the support to step up as the role expands. This role requires a hands-on leader who likes being close to the numbers.

What You'll Own

Lead a two-person accounting team, managing our Senior Accountant and supporting the development of the Accountant on their team
Work with the team to put scalable internal controls in place for accurate, reliable financial statements
Own cash and cashflow planning across short- and long-term horizons
Partner with the executive team to build annual budgets, forecasts, and department-specific KPI reporting
Build financial models and scenario plans to support strategic decisions and fundraising
Support the CEO on investor materials and Board and shareholder reporting
Manage tax, audit, legal, and banking partners, and keep FORM compliant across jurisdictions

What Great Looks Like

Reliable reporting generated in hours, not days
A controls environment the executive team trusts
Budgets and KPI reports that department leads use to run their teams
AI embedded in our finance workflows, so the team spends less time on manual tasks and more on insights

The Landscape

Inventory across multi-warehouse global operations 
Multiple entities (Canada and US) and multiple currencies
Startup financing, including SAFEs, convertible notes, and equity and debt rounds

How We Work

Daring -
Greatness lies just outside our comfort zone. You bring fresh ideas and aren't afraid to try something new.
Focused -
We're not afraid of throwing out great ideas to execute the right one. You know which numbers matter most and keep the team pointed at them.
Human -
Work as a team, work for one another, listen to our members. You make finance approachable and explain the numbers so every FORMie can act on them.
Learn Fast, Act Fast
- Improve through trial, testing and action. You move with urgency, learn from each cycle, and keep improving how finance works.

Requirements

Required Skills & Qualifications

CPA or equivalent, with 7-10 years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including leading and developing a team in a Director-level role at a growing startup
Experience with hardware and SaaS business models, including a strong understanding of SaaS KPIs

Strong financial modelling skills and the ability to turn data into decisions
A proven record of accurate internal and external financial and KPI reporting in a complex, multi-currency environment
Experience with employee stock option plans (ESOPs), including administration and cap table management
Experience supporting equity and debt financing processes
Canadian, US, and international tax and accounting experience, including Canadian grants and tax credits such as SR&ED
Strong storytelling skills that turn financial data into insights people can act on

Nice to Haves

International (US and Europe preferred)
Consumer electronics, fitness, or wearables experience

Benefits

Extended Healthcare Plan (Medical, Disability, Dental & Vision)
Group Life - AD&D - Critical Illness Insurance
Paid Time Off Benefits
Employee Discounts
Employee Assistance Program - Counselling

This role has an annual salary range of  $135,000 to $170,000
. Most new hires do not start at the top of the range. Compensation is determined based on a candidate's experience, skills, qualifications, and overall alignment with the role.
Candidates who are newer to this level of responsibility but demonstrate strong potential may receive an offer toward the lower end of the range. Offers at the higher end are typically reserved for candidates with extensive, directly relevant experience and a proven track record of success in comparable roles and environments.

If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

As part of our store support team, your work directly impacts stores across the country and drives the value that our customers see on the shelves.

We’re looking for people who are passionate about retail and motivated by meaningful work that makes a real impact. This posting represents a current opportunity at Giant Tiger.

Job Title

Head of Merchandise Operations & Financial Planning

About This Role

Giant Tiger is looking for a strategic merchandise leader to help shape the next chapter of our business as we strengthen our position as a Hard Discount retailer.

This is a significant merchandising leadership role with the opportunity to influence how Giant Tiger plans, operates and delivers value to Canadians. Reporting into our Executive Vice President and Chief Merchant, you will lead Merchandise Operations and Financial Planning, establishing the financial plans, operating rhythms and decision-making frameworks that guide our merchandising business. From sales, margin and inventory planning to pricing, promotions and space productivity, you will help ensure our merchandising strategies translate into disciplined execution, profitable growth and consistently low prices our customers can trust.

Giant Tiger operates differently than Canada's largest retailers. We are a Canadian-owned retailer with more than 260 stores, including a significant franchise network. Our success depends on keeping things simple, making disciplined decisions and ensuring our strategies can be executed consistently across our stores.

This role will follow a hybrid remote/onsite schedule. Applicants for this role can expect to work on-site from our Ottawa, Ontario Head Office throughout the month.

What You'll Be Doing

Develop Giant Tiger’s three-year rolling merchandise financial plan and annual fiscal plan to align sales, gross margin, inventory, pricing and other merchandise KPIs with approved strategic and financial priorities.

Veritree And Job Overview

veritree is an award-winning climate tech start-up based in Vancouver. Launched in 2021, our technology measures and verifies the impact of global restoration efforts from the ground up. We are on a mission to plant 1 billion verified trees by 2030, collaborating with businesses, planting organizations, and consumers who believe in the transformative power of verified restoration projects to create real and meaningful impact for the planet, nature, and people.

veritree is seeking a Director, Operations to lead our Operations team: the glue that connects our teams and initiatives. Reporting to the COO, you will own veritree's Revenue Ops, Supply Ops, Business Ops, and Business Intelligence functions. These functions empower our Revenue, Forests, Product & Engineering, and Finance teams to operate as one business.

We sell verified trees sourced from planting partners worldwide, alongside new business lines in carbon, monitoring technology licensing, and nonprofit programs. That makes our business closer to a two-sided marketplace than pure SaaS: every customer commitment depends on supply, delivery, and data lining up behind it. As we move to a new AI-native platform, our Operations team is evolving into a team of operations engineers who build the tools, automations, and data flows the business runs on.

This is a hands-on role: you'll run operations first and then evolve the systems behind it. You inherit a capable team and working systems (several of which we've outgrown) and leave behind infrastructure the rest of the company can build upon. The role starts at Director-level, with room for advancement as determined by job performance and business needs.

12 Month Key Outcomes (12m KOs)

Take the wheel: within your first 90 days, run the weekly operations cadence, own escalations across all four functions, and become the decision-maker on operational calls
Operating rhythm: set up how Operations runs for the next stage of the company: a clear meeting rhythm, defined team roles/decision rights, one agreed definition and owner for core metrics (pipeline, ACV, NRR, gross margin, tree inventory), and a 12-month operations roadmap signed off by executive leadership
Trusted data and reporting: keep commercial and delivery data clean across HubSpot, NetSuite, and the platform through go-live and beyond, and produce the monthly reporting pack and the operational metrics in board reporting from the BI stack
AI and automation: ship AI-powered tools and automations that measurably reduce manual work and save costs across the business

Cross-Functional Operations

Run the operating cadence (meeting cadences, monthly business reviews, semi-annual planning) and the forums where Revenue, Forests, and Product & Engineering align on priorities

Own the intake, prioritization, and SLA framework for operations requests from every team
Own operational readiness on the platform after go-live: close workflow gaps with Product & Engineering and lead change management
Make operational and commercial decisions within agreed guardrails (pricing, margin floors, custom deliverables), and escalate exceptions to executive leadership with a clear recommendation

Team Leadership & Development

Lead, coach, and develop the Operations team, including managers and individual contributors
Own hiring, onboarding, and ongoing performance management, in partnership with People Operations
Evolve the team into operations engineers by defining roles and scopes and building a culture that is both high-accountability and high-support

Own lead and sales funnel, retention, and unit-economics reporting

Business Operations

Run the OKR process and tracker, and support annual operating planning
Own the operating model for customer and partner site visits

Business Intelligence & Reporting

Direct the team's AI agenda, shipping internal tools, agents, and workflow automations that measurably increase output across the business

Professional Requirements Or Qualifications

8+ years in operations, including 3+ years leading a multi-function operations team (at least Revenue Operations and Business Operations) at a B2B company of roughly 75 to 250 people
Experience taking a company from founder-led, ad hoc operations to a repeatable operating system

Experience designing operating processes (intake, SLAs, deal desk) and leading change management for systems people use every day

Personal Strengths

An operator first: hands-on and low ego

jobs.title: Revenue Performance Director
jobs.description:
Dayforce is a global human capital management (HCM) company headquartered in Toronto, Ontario, and Minneapolis, Minnesota, with operations across North America, Europe, Middle East, Africa (EMEA), and the Asia Pacific Japan (APJ) region.

Our award-winning Cloud HCM platform offers a unified solution database and continuous calculation engine, driving efficiency, productivity and compliance for the global workforce.

Our brand promise - Makes Work Life Better™ - Reflects our commitment to employees, customers, partners and communities globally.

About The Opportunity

The Revenue Performance Director is a strategic performance advisor embedded within a North American sales segment, accountable for helping leadership identify where execution is constraining revenue performance and mobilizing the capabilities required to improve it.

Working at the intersection of sales strategy, enablement, coaching, operations, and execution, the role connects signals from pipeline, forecast, customer conversations, seller behavior, and leadership priorities to identify performance gaps and recommend focused responses.

This role is designed for a commercially minded partner who can develop a clear point of view, mobilize the right resources, and help sales leaders reinforce the behaviors and operating rhythms that improve pipeline health, conversion, win rate, forecast confidence, and seller productivity.

Success is measured by meaningful movement in the business, not simply by the volume of programs or content delivered.

What You’ll Get To Do

Serve as a trusted revenue performance advisor to the segment’s senior sales leader and leadership team, bringing an informed perspective on execution priorities and performance gaps and building support for the actions required to improve performance.
Develop a fact-based view of segment performance by connecting insights from Salesforce, Gong, pipeline and forecast reviews, win/loss analysis, customer conversations, seller behavior, and market conditions.
Translate complex or competing signals into clear recommendations about what is happening, why it matters, where leaders should focus, and how progress will be measured.
Partner with sales leadership to create and manage a focused quarterly roadmap tied to the segment’s most important commercial outcomes.
Diagnose the root causes of execution gaps and determine the most appropriate response, including leader coaching, seller activation, process reinforcement, targeted skill development, strategic deal support, or improved adoption of existing resources.
Translate sales strategy into observable seller and manager behaviors that can be coached, reinforced, and inspected.
Mobilize and, when needed, facilitate targeted coaching, leadership sessions, deal interventions, or skill development based on validated performance needs, leveraging specialist RAP expertise where appropriate.
Orchestrate across Sales, Revenue Operations, Marketing, Product, Curriculum and Architecture, Competitive Intelligence, Value Advisory, Solution Consulting, and Customer Success to deliver coordinated support to the field.
Reinforce effective use of Dayforce’s sales methodology, systems, tools, and operating practices, including Salesforce, Gong, Joint Execution Plans, digital sales rooms, and AI-enabled workflows.
Establish success measures for roadmap priorities, inspect progress, adjust interventions based on evidence, and help scale effective practices across the broader organization.
Act as a gatekeeper for segment activation, helping leaders prioritize competing requests, protect seller capacity, and make explicit tradeoffs based on expected business impact.
Connect validated business needs to existing RAP and go-to-market capabilities, reusing and adapting proven solutions before creating new interventions.
Identify performance gaps and winning patterns, using evidence to determine what should be addressed, reinforced, or scaled.

How Success Will Be Measured

Success will be measured by the Revenue Performance Director’s ability to identify and prioritize material performance opportunities, mobilize the right response, influence observable changes in seller and leader behavior, and demonstrate a contribution to measurable business outcomes.
Primary business outcomes may include qualified pipeline conversion, stage progression, qualified win rate, forecast accuracy, sales-cycle velocity, seller productivity, and revenue attainment.
Leading indicators may include executive and buying-committee engagement, manager coaching effectiveness, customer commitment, methodology application, and effective use of priority selling tools.
Measures will be agreed with Sales Leadership based on the specific performance constraint being addressed rather than applying the same KPI set to every segment or initiative.

Skills And Experience We Value

Experience in revenue enablement, sales effectiveness, sales leadership, go-to-market strategy, commercial excellence, or a comparable role supporting a complex B2B sales organization.
Demonstrated ability to partner with senior sales leaders and translate commercial priorities into practical execution plans.
Strong business and financial acumen, with the ability to connect seller behavior and execution quality to pipeline, conversion, sales-cycle progression, forecast confidence, and revenue outcomes.
Experience interpreting quantitative and qualitative performance signals and turning them into a clear point of view and actionable recommendation.
Strong knowledge of enterprise or midmarket sales motions, including qualification, discovery, executive engagement, value articulation, buying-committee management, deal progression, negotiation, and close.
Demonstrated skill in coaching sellers and sales leaders, facilitating high-value working sessions, and constructively challenging assumptions.
Strong executive communication and cross-functional influence, with the confidence to recommend priorities and tradeoffs in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment.
Experience using platforms such as Salesforce and Gong to identify execution patterns, support coaching, and measure behavior or performance change.
Strong planning and execution discipline, with the ability to move from diagnosis through activation and measurement.
Ability to apply AI and emerging revenue technologies to performance diagnosis, seller productivity, coaching, and execution, rather than simply drive adoption of AI tools.

What Would Make You Stand Out

10+ years of experience carrying a quota, leading a sales team, coaching frontline managers, or working within an enterprise SaaS sales organization.
Experience supporting HCM, payroll, workforce management, ERP, or another complex business-technology category.
Familiarity with Challenger, MEDDPICC, value-based selling, mutual action plans, or comparable enterprise sales methodologies.
Experience building business cases, quantifying customer value, or helping sellers engage CFOs and other executive buyers.
A record of producing sustained changes in seller or manager behavior and performance.

What’s In It For You

Dayforce is fueled by the diversity of our talented employees. We are an equal opportunity employer and consider and embrace ALL individuals and what makes them unique. We believe our employees should be happy and healthy, with peace of mind and a sense of fulfillment.

We encourage individuals to apply based on their passions.

Dayforce encourages personal and professional growth. We offer excellent time away from work programs, comprehensive wellness initiatives and recognition through competitive pay and benefits.

With a commitment to community impact, including volunteer days and our charity, Dayforce Cares we provide opportunities for you to thrive both in your career and personal life. Our focus is not just on your job but on supporting you to be the best version of yourself.

About Us

As Canada’s # 1 retailer of cell phones, The Wireless Kiosk @ Costco operates in every Canadian warehouse coast-coast. Our highly trained kiosk Advisors provide unbiased solutions  to some of the most engaged, affluent and loyal consumers in the country. Director Role

Lead leaders. Shape culture. Drive transformation. Build the future!!

We view performance results as an OUTPUT.

OUTPUTS are delivered through actions, behaviors and activity – which we call INPUTS

Too often, we see sales associates and sales managers chasing outputs, which are sometimes known as KPI’s and pushing employees into “closing” customers. We have also seen that this “push” promotes solutions that do not fit what the customer actually needs. This short-term thinking approach we view as unsustainable and does not promote medium to long term growth

Our view is based upon focusing on INPUTS and we are strong believers that if you do the right thing, with the right people, in the right way, at the right time – you will invariably get the right result – the OUTPUT. We also strongly believe that OUTPUTS driven by proper INPUTS, provide the foundation for sustainable on-going growth.

The Director of Retail Operations is a leadership role which requires the right candidate to be able to operate both strategically and tactically (based upon the needs of our business) and is responsible for executing our operational go to market strategy.

Our team across the country is 600+ strong and they are the backbone of our operations. You will be responsible for leading our Western Canadian employees and growing our business through INFLUENCE, building CONSTITUENCY and showing your IMPACT through superior EXECUTION.

The key to winning at retail is the quality of our front-line people. Finding, recruiting, training and successfully onboarding is the foundation of any retailer’s success. This requires us to have hiring clarity on the profile of individual that we are looking for as well as determining who is a suitable candidate and who is not. We have found that this is key to developing and properly casting new hires into roles that match their strengths.

You will report into the Senior Director of Operation and be responsible for leading our business in 40+ locations and will be supporting 3 District Managers. This role requires you to be accountable for creating a high-performance culture where behaviors, execution and results are aligned. You will support our over-arching strategy and with the help of your leadership team, execute the tactical plan developed. You will drive organizational effectiveness (and change, where required) and ensures the creation of sustainable success by developing a strong leadership bench, identifying future talent, and guiding your teams through cyclical periods of growth, transformation, and change.

The ideal candidate must be influential and has impact when they communicate and are able to build constituency with other stakeholders and who can balance strategy with high levels of execution. The ideal candidate will also be able to challenge the status quo, can make difficult decisions, and inspire others to embrace change, while remaining focused and true to the execution of our strategy and operational plan.

Building leadership capability at all levels through coaching, mentorship, and succession planning.
Identifying opportunities to improve productivity, effectiveness, and business outcomes across the region.
Creating a culture of high performance, continuous improvement & accountability
Developing and executing talent strategies that attract, retain, and advance top performers.
Challenging leaders to think differently, improve execution, and raise performance standards.
Strengthening partnerships with Costco leadership through credibility, trust, and a shared commitment to delivering a world-class member experience.

Who You Are

You have 10+ years of progressive leadership experience leading large, multi-site teams through other leaders.
You have a proven track record of improving business performance through people, process, and execution.
You are an exceptional “change leader” who can create alignment, navigate ambiguity, and help teams embrace new ways of working.
You have successfully led organizational transformations, restructures, large-scale business initiatives, or performance turnarounds.
You are skilled at developing District Managers, senior leaders, and high-potential talent.
You hold leaders accountable while maintaining engagement, trust, and strong working relationships.
You inspire trust, create followership, and lead with integrity.
You have demonstrated success building leadership pipelines and developing future-ready organizations.

Your Playground

How You’ll Stand Out

Share examples of leading through significant organizational change while maintaining employee engagement and business performance.
Demonstrate how they have improved underperforming regions, districts, or business units.
Describe how they have built leadership capability and prepared future leaders for advancement.
Showcase examples of transforming team culture and creating sustainable accountability.
Explain how they have influenced senior stakeholders and aligned diverse teams behind a common vision.
Illustrate their approach to succession planning, talent reviews, and leadership development.
Share examples of making difficult decisions that strengthened long-term organizational effectiveness.

Total compensation package - $180K - $200K+
Excellent extended health benefits
RRSP company match program
Discounts on the newest wireless technology and plans

jobs.description:
Overview

The High‑Risk Portfolio Management Team (HRPMT) enhances CCB’s overall risk oversight capabilities by providing specialized expertise, advisory support, and strategic guidance for accounts exhibiting deteriorating financial performance, emerging risk indicators, or complex credit concerns. Unlike traditional credit roles, HRPMT operates in a consulting and advisory capacity
, supporting the commercial banking lines of business with expert insights to strengthen the management of high‑risk, watch‑list, and impaired accounts.

The team works closely with relationship managers, credit partners, and leadership to ensure early identification of risk, informed decision‑making, and strong discipline around the oversight of vulnerable segments of the portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

Specialized Risk Assessment & Advisory Support

Conducts advanced financial analysis and risk assessments of clients demonstrating signs of weakness or deterioration, providing the LOB with actionable insights and recommended risk‑mitigation strategies.
Offers guidance on appropriate structures, terms, and risk controls for high‑risk accounts, ensuring alignment with bank policies, risk appetite, and regulatory expectations.
Advises on complex or distressed credit situations, including covenant breaches, liquidity concerns, operational challenges, and industry‑driven pressures.
Supports LOB teams with strategies for managing watch‑list, impaired, and emerging‑risk accounts, including exit strategies, recovery pathways, and restructuring options.

High‑Risk Portfolio Oversight

Performs enhanced portfolio monitoring to detect early‑warning signals, covenant non‑compliance, or deteriorating credit trends.
Evaluates portfolio‑level performance indicators and risk concentrations, escalating concerns where appropriate and recommending corrective actions.
Assesses the overall quality of risk management practices across the high‑risk portfolio, identifying gaps and recommending improvements.

Subject Matter Expertise & Consultancy

Operates as a specialist resource to senior leaders and frontline teams, supporting decision‑making on complex or ambiguous credit scenarios.
Provides expertise for the review of high‑risk transactions, challenging underlying assumptions, and advising on risk‑aligned alternatives.
Engages with internal stakeholders to ensure consistency in the management of high‑risk exposures across the enterprise.

Governance, Reporting & Continuous Improvement

Strengthens discipline and transparency around watch‑list and impaired account management procedures.
Implements adjustments to risk oversight strategies in response to shifting market, economic, or client‑specific conditions.
Contributes to enterprise initiatives that enhance risk governance, improve monitoring capabilities, and support proactive portfolio management.

Stakeholder Engagement

Partners closely with Commercial banking stakeholders to support their management of deteriorating clients while maintaining LOB ownership of BAU underwriting and client relationships.
Supports senior leadership with insights, analysis, and recommendations to inform capital allocation decisions and risk appetite considerations.
Engages with industry peers and internal networks to stay informed on emerging risks, competitive trends, and evolving best practices.

Qualifications

7+ years of experience in credit, lending, restructuring, portfolio management, or financial analysis within a corporate or banking environment.
Strong credit qualifications, including deep knowledge of commercial credit structures, deteriorating‑credit dynamics, and high‑risk portfolio management practices.
Bachelor’s degree required; master’s degree preferred (Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, or related field).
Demonstrated ability to assess complex financial situations, identify risks, and recommend solutions aligned with risk appetite and enterprise policies.
Proven capability to operate in an advisory role, influence stakeholders, and provide expertise in non‑routine, ambiguous, or sensitive credit situations.
Strong analytical, communication, and problem‑solving skills with the ability to apply sound judgment under pressure.

Overview

The High‑Risk Portfolio Management Team (HRPMT) enhances CCB’s overall risk oversight capabilities by providing specialized expertise, advisory support, and strategic guidance for accounts exhibiting deteriorating financial performance, emerging risk indicators, or complex credit concerns. Unlike traditional credit roles, HRPMT operates in a consulting and advisory capacity
, supporting the commercial banking lines of business with expert insights to strengthen the management of high‑risk, watch‑list, and impaired accounts.

The team works closely with relationship managers, credit partners, and leadership to ensure early identification of risk, informed decision‑making, and strong discipline around the oversight of vulnerable segments of the portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

Specialized Risk Assessment & Advisory Support

Conducts advanced financial analysis and risk assessments of clients demonstrating signs of weakness or deterioration, providing the LOB with actionable insights and recommended risk‑mitigation strategies.
Offers guidance on appropriate structures, terms, and risk controls for high‑risk accounts, ensuring alignment with bank policies, risk appetite, and regulatory expectations.
Advises on complex or distressed credit situations, including covenant breaches, liquidity concerns, operational challenges, and industry‑driven pressures.
Supports LOB teams with strategies for managing watch‑list, impaired, and emerging‑risk accounts, including exit strategies, recovery pathways, and restructuring options.

High‑Risk Portfolio Oversight

Performs enhanced portfolio monitoring to detect early‑warning signals, covenant non‑compliance, or deteriorating credit trends.
Evaluates portfolio‑level performance indicators and risk concentrations, escalating concerns where appropriate and recommending corrective actions.
Assesses the overall quality of risk management practices across the high‑risk portfolio, identifying gaps and recommending improvements.

Subject Matter Expertise & Consultancy

Operates as a specialist resource to senior leaders and frontline teams, supporting decision‑making on complex or ambiguous credit scenarios.
Provides expertise for the review of high‑risk transactions, challenging underlying assumptions, and advising on risk‑aligned alternatives.
Engages with internal stakeholders to ensure consistency in the management of high‑risk exposures across the enterprise.

Governance, Reporting & Continuous Improvement

Strengthens discipline and transparency around watch‑list and impaired account management procedures.
Implements adjustments to risk oversight strategies in response to shifting market, economic, or client‑specific conditions.
Contributes to enterprise initiatives that enhance risk governance, improve monitoring capabilities, and support proactive portfolio management.

Stakeholder Engagement

Partners closely with Commercial banking stakeholders to support their management of deteriorating clients while maintaining LOB ownership of BAU underwriting and client relationships.
Supports senior leadership with insights, analysis, and recommendations to inform capital allocation decisions and risk appetite considerations.
Engages with industry peers and internal networks to stay informed on emerging risks, competitive trends, and evolving best practices.

Qualifications

7+ years of experience in credit, lending, restructuring, portfolio management, or financial analysis within a corporate or banking environment.
Strong credit qualifications, including deep knowledge of commercial credit structures, deteriorating‑credit dynamics, and high‑risk portfolio management practices.
Bachelor’s degree required; master’s degree preferred (Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, or related field).
Demonstrated ability to assess complex financial situations, identify risks, and recommend solutions aligned with risk appetite and enterprise policies.
Proven capability to operate in an advisory role, influence stakeholders, and provide expertise in non‑routine, ambiguous, or sensitive credit situations.
Strong analytical, communication, and problem‑solving skills with the ability to apply sound judgment under pressure.

About The Job

The Director, IT & Data Business Partner (BP) serves as the strategic liaison between Danone Canada’s enterprise functions and the IT & Data organization. This role partners closely with stakeholders across Commercial, Sales, Marketing, eCommerce, Insights, Strategy & Transformation, Operations, Supply Chain, Research & Innovation (R&I), Quality, Food Safety & Compliance (QFS), Cycles & Procurement (C&P), Finance, HR, Legal, Customer Care, and supporting functions to understand business priorities, translate needs into technology and data solutions, and drive value realization through product adoption and delivery.

The Director BP is responsible for aligning Canada business objectives with IT & Data product roadmaps, ensuring that strategic initiatives are prioritized, funded, governed, and successfully executed. Acting as a trusted advisor, this role connects Canadian business leaders with Product Groups, Product Owners, chapters, regional teams, and global technology partners to accelerate innovation, improve enterprise performance, and support business transformation.

This position plays a critical role in driving business engagement, ensuring service continuity, strengthening cyber and data governance, and maximizing the value delivered through technology, data, analytics, automation, AI, digital products, and enterprise platforms across Danone Canada.

Key Responsibilities

Business Partnership & Strategic Alignment

Serve as the primary IT & Data partner for Danone Canada leaders across enterprise functions, including Commercial, Sales, Marketing, eCommerce, Insights, Strategy & Transformation, Operations, Supply Chain, R&I, QFS, C&P, Finance, HR, Legal, Customer Care, and supporting functions.
Develop a deep understanding of Canada business priorities, challenges, market dynamics, and strategic objectives.
Translate business needs into technology, data, analytics, automation, AI, and enterprise platform opportunities and connect stakeholders with the appropriate Product Groups and subject matter experts.
Facilitate prioritization of Canadian business initiatives and ensure alignment with global, regional, and local IT & Data strategies.
Build and maintain strong relationships with business stakeholders to foster trust, collaboration, accountable ownership, and value creation.

Portfolio & Roadmap Management

Manage the Canada IT & Data product and project portfolio in partnership with Product Groups, chapters, regional IT & Data teams, and global technology partners.
Develop and maintain an enterprise Canada roadmap that aligns technology capabilities with business priorities across the full value chain.
Support business case development, CAPEX/OPEX planning, demand intake, and investment prioritization for strategic initiatives.
Ensure visibility, alignment, and communication of priorities across Canada business leadership, regional IT & Data, Product Groups, and delivery teams.

Value Creation & Business Outcomes

Identify opportunities to leverage technology, digital capabilities, enterprise platforms, data, analytics, automation, and AI to improve business performance and enterprise outcomes across Danone Canada.
Drive adoption of products and solutions to maximize business value realization, including self-service analytics, data products, Copilot and AI capabilities, workflow automation, and fit-for-purpose tools.
Monitor business satisfaction and continuously identify opportunities to improve service delivery, user experience, process efficiency, and decision-making.
Support business continuity by partnering with Product Groups, IT4U, cybersecurity, infrastructure, data, and application teams to address risks, escalations, critical issues, and local market needs.

Product Delivery & Transformation

Collaborate with Product Owners and Product Group Leaders throughout the product lifecycle, from ideation through feasibility, funding, delivery, deployment, adoption, and continuous improvement.
Ensure business requirements, success metrics, value assumptions, governance needs, data ownership, and expected outcomes are clearly defined.
Promote agile ways of working and support effective product ownership, demand governance, business case discipline, and adoption practices.
Lead cross-functional alignment across Canada, regional, and global teams to support successful delivery of strategic initiatives across commercial, operations, supply chain, finance, HR, digital, data, and supporting functions.

Stakeholder Management & Communication

Act as a trusted advisor and advocate for Danone Canada within the IT & Data organization.
Provide regular updates on roadmap progress, business priorities, key initiatives, risks, funding needs, service topics, and opportunities.
Facilitate discussions and decision-making across multiple stakeholders and functions, including Canadian leadership forums, Product Groups, project steercos, and business-led governance forums.
Promote continuous improvement and strengthen collaboration between Canada business teams and IT & Data teams, positioning IT & Data as a strategic partner and co-owner of business outcomes.

Compensation, Benefits & Hiring Transparency

The annual base salary range for this position is $140,000 to $190,000 CAD. The final salary offered will be determined by factors such as relevant experience and qualifications, internal equity and external market conditions.

Danone Canada also offers a competitive short-term incentive bonus and a comprehensive benefits package, including group insurance, group retirement plans, wellbeing account, flexible time off, true hybrid work environment, paid parental leave, and other attractive options.

7+ years of experience in technology, digital, data, business partnering, product management, enterprise applications, or related business transformation roles.
Experience working across commercial, sales, marketing, eCommerce, strategy, operations, supply chain, procurement, quality, R&I, finance, HR, or related enterprise functions preferred.
Proven experience managing stakeholders and influencing decisions across multiple organizational levels, including senior business leaders.
Experience participating in product-centric, agile, digital transformation, data governance, AI, automation, or enterprise technology environments.

Skills & Competencies

Strong business partnering and stakeholder management capabilities across enterprise functions.
Ability to translate business challenges into technology, data, analytics, automation, AI, and enterprise platform solutions.
Excellent communication, facilitation, change management, and influencing skills.
Strong project, portfolio, roadmap, demand, funding, and prioritization management capabilities.
Solid understanding of product management, agile delivery methodologies, data governance, cybersecurity, enterprise applications, and service management.
Ability to manage complex situations and navigate ambiguity in a fast-paced, matrixed environment.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a focus on delivering measurable business outcomes.
Demonstrated ability to work effectively across local, regional, and global teams.

Assets

Experience within CPG, FMCG, manufacturing, retail, commercial, supply chain, or enterprise business environments.
Understanding of enterprise data and analytics, retailer data, commercial platforms, digital marketing and eCommerce tools, finance and supporting function processes, supply chain systems, quality systems, operational analytics, procurement platforms, automation, AI, and enterprise business processes.
Experience working in a global matrix organization and partnering with local market leadership, regional IT & Data teams, Product Groups, and global technology teams.

About us

Danone Canada is part of Danone, the largest certified B Corp™ in the world, proudly using our business as a force for good – creating value for people, communities, and the planet. Guided by our long-standing mission to bring health through food to as many people as possible
