new_jobs.description:
Dayforce is a global human capital management (HCM) company headquartered in Toronto, Ontario, and Minneapolis, Minnesota, with operations across North America, Europe, Middle East, Africa (EMEA), and the Asia Pacific Japan (APJ) region.

Our award-winning Cloud HCM platform offers a unified solution database and continuous calculation engine, driving efficiency, productivity and compliance for the global workforce.

Our brand promise - Makes Work Life Better™ - Reflects our commitment to employees, customers, partners and communities globally.

About The Opportunity

The Revenue Performance Director is a strategic performance advisor embedded within a North American sales segment, accountable for helping leadership identify where execution is constraining revenue performance and mobilizing the capabilities required to improve it.

Working at the intersection of sales strategy, enablement, coaching, operations, and execution, the role connects signals from pipeline, forecast, customer conversations, seller behavior, and leadership priorities to identify performance gaps and recommend focused responses.

This role is designed for a commercially minded partner who can develop a clear point of view, mobilize the right resources, and help sales leaders reinforce the behaviors and operating rhythms that improve pipeline health, conversion, win rate, forecast confidence, and seller productivity.

Success is measured by meaningful movement in the business, not simply by the volume of programs or content delivered.

What You’ll Get To Do

Serve as a trusted revenue performance advisor to the segment’s senior sales leader and leadership team, bringing an informed perspective on execution priorities and performance gaps and building support for the actions required to improve performance.
Develop a fact-based view of segment performance by connecting insights from Salesforce, Gong, pipeline and forecast reviews, win/loss analysis, customer conversations, seller behavior, and market conditions.
Translate complex or competing signals into clear recommendations about what is happening, why it matters, where leaders should focus, and how progress will be measured.
Partner with sales leadership to create and manage a focused quarterly roadmap tied to the segment’s most important commercial outcomes.
Diagnose the root causes of execution gaps and determine the most appropriate response, including leader coaching, seller activation, process reinforcement, targeted skill development, strategic deal support, or improved adoption of existing resources.
Translate sales strategy into observable seller and manager behaviors that can be coached, reinforced, and inspected.
Mobilize and, when needed, facilitate targeted coaching, leadership sessions, deal interventions, or skill development based on validated performance needs, leveraging specialist RAP expertise where appropriate.
Orchestrate across Sales, Revenue Operations, Marketing, Product, Curriculum and Architecture, Competitive Intelligence, Value Advisory, Solution Consulting, and Customer Success to deliver coordinated support to the field.
Reinforce effective use of Dayforce’s sales methodology, systems, tools, and operating practices, including Salesforce, Gong, Joint Execution Plans, digital sales rooms, and AI-enabled workflows.
Establish success measures for roadmap priorities, inspect progress, adjust interventions based on evidence, and help scale effective practices across the broader organization.
Act as a gatekeeper for segment activation, helping leaders prioritize competing requests, protect seller capacity, and make explicit tradeoffs based on expected business impact.
Connect validated business needs to existing RAP and go-to-market capabilities, reusing and adapting proven solutions before creating new interventions.
Identify performance gaps and winning patterns, using evidence to determine what should be addressed, reinforced, or scaled.

How Success Will Be Measured

Success will be measured by the Revenue Performance Director’s ability to identify and prioritize material performance opportunities, mobilize the right response, influence observable changes in seller and leader behavior, and demonstrate a contribution to measurable business outcomes.
Primary business outcomes may include qualified pipeline conversion, stage progression, qualified win rate, forecast accuracy, sales-cycle velocity, seller productivity, and revenue attainment.
Leading indicators may include executive and buying-committee engagement, manager coaching effectiveness, customer commitment, methodology application, and effective use of priority selling tools.
Measures will be agreed with Sales Leadership based on the specific performance constraint being addressed rather than applying the same KPI set to every segment or initiative.

Experience in revenue enablement, sales effectiveness, sales leadership, go-to-market strategy, commercial excellence, or a comparable role supporting a complex B2B sales organization.
Demonstrated ability to partner with senior sales leaders and translate commercial priorities into practical execution plans.
Strong business and financial acumen, with the ability to connect seller behavior and execution quality to pipeline, conversion, sales-cycle progression, forecast confidence, and revenue outcomes.
Experience interpreting quantitative and qualitative performance signals and turning them into a clear point of view and actionable recommendation.
Strong knowledge of enterprise or midmarket sales motions, including qualification, discovery, executive engagement, value articulation, buying-committee management, deal progression, negotiation, and close.
Demonstrated skill in coaching sellers and sales leaders, facilitating high-value working sessions, and constructively challenging assumptions.
Strong executive communication and cross-functional influence, with the confidence to recommend priorities and tradeoffs in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment.
Experience using platforms such as Salesforce and Gong to identify execution patterns, support coaching, and measure behavior or performance change.
Strong planning and execution discipline, with the ability to move from diagnosis through activation and measurement.
Ability to apply AI and emerging revenue technologies to performance diagnosis, seller productivity, coaching, and execution, rather than simply drive adoption of AI tools.

10+ years of experience carrying a quota, leading a sales team, coaching frontline managers, or working within an enterprise SaaS sales organization.
Experience supporting HCM, payroll, workforce management, ERP, or another complex business-technology category.
Familiarity with Challenger, MEDDPICC, value-based selling, mutual action plans, or comparable enterprise sales methodologies.
Experience building business cases, quantifying customer value, or helping sellers engage CFOs and other executive buyers.
A record of producing sustained changes in seller or manager behavior and performance.

Dayforce is fueled by the diversity of our talented employees. We are an equal opportunity employer and consider and embrace ALL individuals and what makes them unique. We believe our employees should be happy and healthy, with peace of mind and a sense of fulfillment.

We encourage individuals to apply based on their passions.

Overview

The High‑Risk Portfolio Management Team (HRPMT) enhances CCB’s overall risk oversight capabilities by providing specialized expertise, advisory support, and strategic guidance for accounts exhibiting deteriorating financial performance, emerging risk indicators, or complex credit concerns. Unlike traditional credit roles, HRPMT operates in a consulting and advisory capacity
, supporting the commercial banking lines of business with expert insights to strengthen the management of high‑risk, watch‑list, and impaired accounts.

The team works closely with relationship managers, credit partners, and leadership to ensure early identification of risk, informed decision‑making, and strong discipline around the oversight of vulnerable segments of the portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

Specialized Risk Assessment & Advisory Support

Conducts advanced financial analysis and risk assessments of clients demonstrating signs of weakness or deterioration, providing the LOB with actionable insights and recommended risk‑mitigation strategies.
Offers guidance on appropriate structures, terms, and risk controls for high‑risk accounts, ensuring alignment with bank policies, risk appetite, and regulatory expectations.
Advises on complex or distressed credit situations, including covenant breaches, liquidity concerns, operational challenges, and industry‑driven pressures.
Supports LOB teams with strategies for managing watch‑list, impaired, and emerging‑risk accounts, including exit strategies, recovery pathways, and restructuring options.

High‑Risk Portfolio Oversight

Performs enhanced portfolio monitoring to detect early‑warning signals, covenant non‑compliance, or deteriorating credit trends.
Evaluates portfolio‑level performance indicators and risk concentrations, escalating concerns where appropriate and recommending corrective actions.
Assesses the overall quality of risk management practices across the high‑risk portfolio, identifying gaps and recommending improvements.

Subject Matter Expertise & Consultancy

Operates as a specialist resource to senior leaders and frontline teams, supporting decision‑making on complex or ambiguous credit scenarios.
Provides expertise for the review of high‑risk transactions, challenging underlying assumptions, and advising on risk‑aligned alternatives.
Engages with internal stakeholders to ensure consistency in the management of high‑risk exposures across the enterprise.

Governance, Reporting & Continuous Improvement

Strengthens discipline and transparency around watch‑list and impaired account management procedures.
Implements adjustments to risk oversight strategies in response to shifting market, economic, or client‑specific conditions.
Contributes to enterprise initiatives that enhance risk governance, improve monitoring capabilities, and support proactive portfolio management.

Stakeholder Engagement

Partners closely with Commercial banking stakeholders to support their management of deteriorating clients while maintaining LOB ownership of BAU underwriting and client relationships.
Supports senior leadership with insights, analysis, and recommendations to inform capital allocation decisions and risk appetite considerations.
Engages with industry peers and internal networks to stay informed on emerging risks, competitive trends, and evolving best practices.

Qualifications

7+ years of experience in credit, lending, restructuring, portfolio management, or financial analysis within a corporate or banking environment.
Strong credit qualifications, including deep knowledge of commercial credit structures, deteriorating‑credit dynamics, and high‑risk portfolio management practices.
Bachelor’s degree required; master’s degree preferred (Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, or related field).
Demonstrated ability to assess complex financial situations, identify risks, and recommend solutions aligned with risk appetite and enterprise policies.
Proven capability to operate in an advisory role, influence stakeholders, and provide expertise in non‑routine, ambiguous, or sensitive credit situations.
Strong analytical, communication, and problem‑solving skills with the ability to apply sound judgment under pressure.

VP sales Lead , Commercial Banking

Lead Growth. Influence Strategy. Help Businesses Thrive.

At BMO Commercial Bank, we're looking for a proven relationship management leader to drive growth across a portfolio of sophisticated commercial clients. In this role, you'll serve as a trusted advisor to business owners, executives, and key decision-makers, helping them navigate opportunities, manage risk, and achieve their long-term strategic objectives.

As a senior member of the Commercial Banking team, you'll lead complex financing transactions, champion client relationships, and play a pivotal role in expanding BMO's presence in the market. You'll work alongside industry specialists, credit partners, and senior leaders to deliver customized financial solutions that help businesses grow and succeed.

What You'll Do

Drive Business Growth

Develop and execute market growth strategies to expand BMO's commercial banking presence.
Build and deepen relationships with high-value clients and prospective businesses.
Identify new business opportunities and grow market share through proactive networking, referrals, and strategic relationship development.
Maximize client potential by delivering integrated banking, treasury, cash management, and lending solutions.

Lead Complex Commercial Transactions

Structure and negotiate sophisticated credit facilities and financial solutions.
Lead high-value financing opportunities from initial discussion through approval and closing.
Partner with credit, risk, and product teams to deliver tailored solutions that meet client objectives while maintaining sound risk practices.
Act as the primary client advocate throughout the transaction process.

Serve as a Trusted Strategic Advisor

Build lasting relationships with business owners, executives, and industry leaders.
Provide strategic guidance on financing structures, growth opportunities, acquisitions, succession planning, and capital needs.
Monitor industry trends, market dynamics, and emerging opportunities to deliver valuable insights to clients.
Resolve complex client issues while maintaining exceptional client experience and engagement.

Collaborate Across the Enterprise

Work closely with senior leaders and cross-functional partners to deliver holistic solutions.
Leverage the full capabilities of BMO to support client growth and strengthen relationships.
Represent BMO within the business community, industry associations, and market events.

Lead and Develop High-Performing Teams

Inspire, coach, and develop a team of banking professionals.
Foster a collaborative, inclusive, and performance-driven culture.
Support talent development, succession planning, and employee growth.
Lead through change and help teams adapt to evolving client and market needs.

What You'll Bring

10+ years of experience in Commercial Banking, Corporate Banking, Relationship Management, or a comparable client-facing financial services environment.
Demonstrated success managing and growing complex commercial client portfolios.
Strong commercial credit expertise, including structuring, negotiating, and underwriting complex financing transactions.
Proven business development track record and ability to build trusted executive-level relationships.
Strong leadership experience with demonstrated success coaching and developing talent.
Deep understanding of financial analysis, risk assessment, and portfolio management.
Excellent communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills.
Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Why Join BMO?

Manage sophisticated client relationships and impactful commercial transactions.
Influence business growth strategies across a dynamic market.
Collaborate with industry-leading banking professionals and specialists.
Access meaningful career development and leadership opportunities.
Join a purpose-driven organization committed to Boldly Growing the Good in business and life.

If you're passionate about relationship management, business development, and helping Canadian businesses achieve their ambitions, we invite you to explore this opportunity with BMO Commercial Bank.

new_jobs.title: Director, Corporate and Commercial Credit Risk
new_jobs.description:
Provides independent, objective review and adjudication of credit applications and transactions for an assigned portfolio within credit limits or makes credit recommendations and escalates as required. Ensures the credit quality of the assigned portfolios are maintained within the Bank’s risk tolerance, policies & procedures, and meet financing guidelines. Supports credit adjudication operations and initiatives. Provides training and support to teams and channels where the applications and transactions originate.

Works with stakeholders to ensure effectiveness of risk management controls, analysis and monitoring on a transactional and portfolio basis.
Provides credit coaching, training and support to direct team and other stakeholders as required.
Provides strategic input into business decisions as a trusted advisor.
Makes recommendations to senior leaders on strategy and new initiatives, based on an in-depth understanding of the business/group.
Acts as a subject matter expert on relevant regulations and policies.
May network with industry contacts to gain competitive insights and best practices.
Influences and negotiates to achieve business objectives.
Identifies emerging issues and trends to inform decision-making.
Recommends business priorities, advises on resource requirements and develops roadmap for strategic execution.
Manages resources and leads the execution of strategic initiatives to deliver on business and financial goals.
Conducts independent analysis and assessment to resolve strategic issues.
Acts as the prime subject matter expert for internal/external stakeholders.
Ensures alignment between stakeholders.
Develops and manages comprehensive information management systems; designs and/or leads initiatives to improve processes, analysis and reporting.
Integrates information from multiple sources to enable more efficient processes, enhanced analysis and/or streamlined reporting.
Defines business requirements for analytics & reporting to ensure data insights inform business decision making.
Employs systems (e.g. customized exception reports, tracking reports etc.) to manage information.
Breaks down strategic problems, and analyses data and information to provide insights and recommendations.
Leads change management programs of varying scope and type, including readiness assessments, planning, stakeholder management, execution, evaluation and sustainment of initiatives.
Leads the development of the communication strategy focusing on positively influencing or changing behaviour.
Collaborates across BMO to develop communications strategies and ensure consistency of messaging, in order to positively influence or change behaviour.
Leads the execution of operational programs; assesses and adapts as needed to ensure quality of execution.
Supports credit due diligence activities for bank acquisitions or integration.
Reviews and communicates decisions on credit transactions with rationale that can be understood and explained to customers.
Identifies and advises on terms, conditions and collateral requirements for the transaction decision as well as opportunities for cross-selling and/or alternative solutions to meet client’s needs.
Keeps abreast of economic and market developments within the portfolio to inform decision making and credit risk policies.
Provides approval for exceptions according to established policy and standards.
Monitors the credit portfolio through transaction review & approval to ensure compliance with the Bank’s lending policies and procedures.
Provides credit risk coaching and advice to sales & service employees to increase awareness of risk, policy, and knowledge of structuring transactions.
Builds effective relationships with internal/external stakeholders.
Gathers and formats data into regular and ad-hoc reports, and dashboards.
Monitors and tracks performance and addresses any issues.
Executes work to deliver timely, accurate, and efficient service.
Operates at a group/enterprise-wide level and serves as a specialist resource to senior leaders and stakeholders.
Applies expertise and thinks creatively to address unique or ambiguous situations and to find solutions to problems that can be complex and non-routine.
Implements changes in response to shifting trends.
Broader work or accountabilities may be assigned as needed.

Qualifications:

Typically 7+ years of relevant experience and post-secondary degree in related field of study or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Credit Qualifications and associated credit knowledge and skills according to the established qualification standards.
In-depth / expert knowledge of banking products & services.
In-depth / expert knowledge of industry trends and regulations.
In-depth / expert knowledge of credit portfolio management policies & procedures, and financing guidelines.
Proven leadership skills and highly developed coaching skills.
Seasoned professional with a combination of education, experience and industry knowledge.
Verbal & written communication skills - In-depth / Expert.
Analytical and problem solving skills - In-depth / Expert.
Influence skills - In-depth / Expert.
Collaboration & team skills; with a focus on cross-group collaboration - In-depth / Expert.
Able to manage ambiguity.
Data driven decision making - In-depth / Expert.
